questions.question: A fraud label arrives 30 days after a transaction. Can that label be a feature for the original transaction-time prediction?
options: No, it was unavailable at prediction time and would leak the outcome
Yes, because it is eventually stored
Yes, if the model is tree-based
Only when the label is standardized
questions.explanation: Feature eligibility is defined at prediction time. A later outcome may be the training label, but it cannot be an input to that earlier prediction.

questions.question: When should an imputer or scaler learn its parameters?
options: After splitting, from the training partition inside each evaluation fold
Before splitting, from the complete dataset
From the test partition only
Separately from every production request
questions.explanation: Learned transformation state must not inspect evaluation evidence. The frozen training-fitted state is then reused everywhere else.

questions.question: Why can event time alone be insufficient for a point-in-time join?
options: An earlier event may have arrived after the prediction and therefore was not usable online
Event time cannot be stored in a table
Every feature requires a future event
Availability time always equals event time
questions.explanation: Late-arriving data may satisfy the event-time cutoff but violate the real information boundary. Availability time captures when the value became usable.

questions.question: A one-hot encoded merchant identifier adds 500 sparse columns and a frequency encoding adds one column with similar holdout quality. What should the team compare next?
options: Stability, unknown-category behavior, serving cost, and important slices
Only training accuracy
Only the number of model parameters
Whether either feature has a colorful chart
questions.explanation: Predictive quality is only one part of the decision. Operational cost, stability, failure behavior, and slice quality determine whether the representation is useful in production.

questions.question: What is training-serving skew?
options: The same named feature has different values because offline and online logic, data, state, or timing diverge
The training job uses more CPU than serving
The model has more features than labels
The validation set is smaller than the training set
questions.explanation: Skew is a semantic mismatch between training and inference inputs. Parity checks on entity-timestamp pairs can detect it directly.

questions.question: Why is feature importance alone insufficient for deciding that a feature should ship?
options: Importance can reflect proxies, correlation, or leakage and says nothing about reproducibility or serving cost
Importance is available only for linear models
Important features never improve holdout quality
Importance automatically proves causality
questions.explanation: A shipping decision needs ablation evidence, protected evaluation, stability, timing correctness, and operational constraints in addition to model importance.
